title: ARLArena: A Unified Framework for Stable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
claim: Our method trains stably and reaches the highest success rate, while competing methods plateau, fluctuate, or collapse during training.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend below, bold highlighted 'ours' curve
description: Two side-by-side line charts show success rate (y-axis, 0 to about 0.9) against training steps (x-axis, 0 to about 185). The left panel is ALFWorld and the right panel is Sokoban, though the panel titles are cropped out. Each panel has seven curves, drawn with different colors and dash styles: DAPO, SAPO, GSPO, EMPG, GIGPO, GRPO, CISPO and SAMPO (Ours). The thick solid dark-blue SAMPO curve rises fastest and ends highest, at about 0.92 on the left and 0.88 on the right. Baselines are thinner and lower. Some of them collapse: SAPO falls to about 0.1 on the left, and CISPO drops to 0 around step 85 on the right. One shared legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the bold blue curve at the top.
caption: Training curves on ALFWorld (left) and Sokoban (right). Our proposed SAMPO achieves the highest success rates on both environments with stable, monotonic improvement throughout training, while baseline methods exhibit varying degrees of instability. These results demonstrate that principled integration of sequence-level clipping, advantage design, and dynamic filtering, as combined in SAMPO, is critical for both training stability and final performance in multi-turn ARL.
abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (ARL) has rapidly gained attention as a promising paradigm for training agents to solve complex, multi-step interactive tasks. Despite encouraging early results, ARL remains highly unstable, often leading to training collapse. This instability limits scalability to larger environments and longer interaction horizons, and constrains systematic exploration of algorithmic design choices. In this paper, we first propose ARLArena, a stable training recipe and systematic analysis framework that examines training stability in a controlled and reproducible setting. ARLArena first constructs a clean and standardized testbed. Then, we decompose policy gradient into four core design dimensions and assess the performance and stability of each dimension. Through this fine-grained analysis, we distill a unified perspective on ARL and propose SAMPO, a stable agentic policy optimization method designed to mitigate the dominant sources of instability in ARL. Empirically, SAMPO achieves consistently stable training and strong performance across diverse agentic tasks. Overall, this study provides a unifying policy gradient perspective for ARL and offers practical guidance for building stable and reproducible LLM-based agent training pipelines.
